en: The Legend of the Elder Sandhita The Chapter on the Elephant (Hatthivagga), Number Six [Verse 1] When the Buddha Kassapa was present in the world, I was a merchant who lived in Benares. I went to the Teacher, the One of Great Wisdom, and offered him a pair of sandals. [Verse 2] Having made that offering, I took refuge in the Three Jewels. For eighty-four thousand years, I lived as a lay follower. [Verse 3] In this final existence, I have been born in a wealthy family. My name is Sandhita; I am well-known throughout the world. [Verse 4] I possess abundant wealth and grain, and I am endowed with many servants. I am honored by the king and the people, and I am free from all illness. [Verse 5] Because of that meritorious deed, I have attained such great glory. By that root of merit, may I attain the state of Buddhahood. [Verse 6] May I be the teacher of gods and humans, the Knower of All Worlds. May I be the Fully Enlightened One, the One Who Brings Peace to the World. [Verse 7] Through this gift of sandals, may I become a Buddha. May I be the Teacher of the World, the One Who Brings Happiness to the World. [Verse 8] May I be the Fully Enlightened One, the One Who Brings Joy to the World. May I be the One Who Brings Peace to the World, the One Who Brings Bliss to the World. [Verse 9] May I be the Fully Enlightened One, the One Who Brings Delight to the World. May I be the One Who Brings Happiness to the World, the One Who Brings Well-being to the World. When the Assattha tree was shining green,
he cultivated a single perception directed toward the Buddha.
that perception which I then obtained—
By the power of that perception,
the destruction of the taints was attained by me.
In the thirteenth aeon from now,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Sandhita spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Sandhita.
